skill: Infer rank or nullity from a description of a column-space basis or parametrized null space, then apply rank + nullity = number of columns.
learner_operation: Easy: distinguish column count n from row count m, count column-basis vectors r, and compute n-r. Moderate: infer ambient dimension n and the dimension k of the displayed linear span, then compute n-k.
reasoning_steps: Identify the number of columns, directly from matrix dimensions (easy) or vector length (moderate).
Determine rank from cardinality of a column-space basis (easy), or nullity from independent spanning vectors (moderate).
Apply rank(A)+nullity(A)=n, subtract the known dimension, and select one integer from five choices.
invariants: The easy description is an explicitly stated basis, not merely a spanning set; 0 <= r <= min(m,n).
The moderate parametrization is homogeneous and its true coefficient-matrix rank is the nullity; parameter count alone is valid only for an injective parametrization.
One radio answer and five distinct integer choices for observed source questions.
Easy and moderate are separate source families; no row reduction or invertibility reasoning is needed in this KP.
permitted_variations: Easy m,n,r may change independently subject to feasibility and comparable small-number counting/subtraction. Fixed example equalities m=r or n-r=3 are incidental.
Eligible easy results include nullity 0,1 and values above 3 where feasible. Non-square orientation and irrelevant row count may vary without changing n-r.
Moderate vector dimension, number of independent parameters, small coefficients, signs, zero coordinates and parameter locations may vary with comparable workload.
Option values and correct position may vary. Bank profiles seen in source must replay, including banks that omit feasible nonanswers.
The easy target nullity and moderate target rank are source-supported fixed task directions; reversing them is not necessary to defeat a shortcut.

difficulty.easy: Column basis count and one subtraction; observed m=3..6,n=5..10,r=2..5.
difficulty.moderate: Extract independent coefficient vectors of 4 or 5 components with 2 or 3 parameters, then subtract.

source_cases.solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

For the given matrix, we have $n=4,$ since this is the number of components in each of the vectors of the null space. 

Also, since 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\{{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\,|\,\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R\}
$$

we conclude that $\text{nullity}(A)=2.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A) & =n \\ \text{rank}(A)+2 & =4 \\ \text{rank}(A) & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
